passages.text: Message from Chairperson Education today extends far beyond academic achievement. It must equip learners with practical skills, critical thinking abilities, creativity, and the confidence to navigate real-world challenges. Skill-based education plays a pivotal role in this transformation by enabling students to apply knowledge meaningfully and develop capabilities that are essential for both employment and life. By engaging with skill-based subjects, students gain hands-on experience in areas such as communication, problem-solving, technical competencies, and vocational practices. This not only enhances their readiness for the workplace but also opens up multiple pathways for career progression immediately after school. Importantly, it nurtures a spirit of self-reliance and encourages entrepreneurial thinking—qualities that are vital in today's dynamic and evolving world. In this context, I am pleased to note CBSE's initiative in developing the “Compendium of Career and Education Pathways After Skill Subjects in Class XII.” This resource comes at a crucial juncture when students are making important decisions about their future. It provides clear visibility into a wide spectrum of

As the landscape of education and employment continues to evolve, the need to align learning with real-world application has become more critical than ever. Skill education is not merely an addition to the academic framework—it is an essential pathway that enables students to translate knowledge into capability and aspiration into opportunity. At CBSE, our focus has been on systematically strengthening this pathway. The introduction of 43 skill subjects at the senior secondary level reflects a conscious effort to provide students with meaningful exposure to diverse domains and emerging industries. These subjects are designed not only to build technical proficiency but also to develop adaptability, problem-solving ability, and a deeper understanding of how different sectors function in practice. The “Compendium of Career and Education Pathways After Skill Subjects in Class XII” is a continuation of this effort. It has been developed as a practical and structured resource to support students at a critical point of transition—from school to higher education and careers. The compendium seeks to bring clarity to the often complex and fragmented information surrounding career options
